items.title: Reviews count the same small evaluations again and again
items.whyItMatters: Very high overlap (claim c3) makes the literature look stronger and more consistent than it is.
items.opportunity: Build a citation matrix, count each primary study once and report conclusions against it.

items.title: Service-use benefits rest on non-randomised comparisons
items.whyItMatters: Frequent attenders referred at a peak will attend less later anyway (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Grade service-use outcomes separately by comparison type.

items.title: People with complex needs
items.whyItMatters: They take most link worker time and may benefit least from short programmes (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Extract subgroup and mechanism findings for complex needs.

items.title: Community sector costs missing
items.whyItMatters: Savings claims ignore the cost of the activities people are referred to.
items.opportunity: Report which reviews counted community costs.

items.title: The last overview is out of date
items.whyItMatters: It searched to 2017, before most controlled studies.
items.opportunity: Search for reviews published from 2017 onward.

errorsFound: A lead recalled by the model carried a boolean in place of a year; it was stored with an unknown year.
One appraisal method score was outside 0 to 100 and was stored as not assessed.
reevaluation: The umbrella review should appraise each review, measure overlap, count primary studies once and grade each outcome separately, with a section on people with complex needs.
summary: Five gaps; overlap and non-randomised service-use evidence are high severity.
